source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Discourage another opinion because it may damage the therapeutic relationship.","B":"Tell the client that only the surgeon can decide whether a second opinion is allowed.","C":"Support the client's choice and help identify how records or referrals can be obtained.","D":"Advise the client to have the operation first and seek another opinion afterward."}}
source_row.rationale: Supporting an informed client choice and helping coordinate information or referral is consistent with nursing advocacy and client rights. Option C is correct. A and B undermine autonomy, and D defeats the purpose of seeking another opinion before an elective decision.
source_row.source_detail: Management of Care — Advocacy/Client Rights activity statements: advocate for client rights and preferences, provide information needed for informed decisions, facilitate referrals/continuity, and collaborate with the care team. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A client wants a second opinion before a major elective operation. Which nursing response is most appropriate?
